meta.title: Semafide: evidence custody for automated valuations

views.label: Execution path
views.note: A lender calls a cascade; the cascade runs a model. Capture at the application boundary exists as an opt-in scaffold that nothing yet requires the cascade to call.

views.label: The gap
views.note: The configuration that produced the valuation sits with the provider and is overwritten on revision. It does not enter the record.

views.label: Custody chain
views.note: Custody places the record outside the party being examined. Witness and custodian are open: who they are is not decided.

views.label: Examination
views.note: Years later, a repurchase review asks what produced the value. The verifier reports what the evidence establishes and what it does not.

views.label: Truth conditions
views.note: What the verifier can establish, and what it refuses to infer. See the proposition cards.

cards.title: What a single record establishes (code/seal/verifier.py)
items: precedence — the evidence commitment predates the run seal naming it. Not that the analysis consumed it.
witness_attestation — an independently trusted witness key signed an observed-execution attestation binding the run, evidence, action, and capture reference. Not a signature over a supplied bundle.
recipe_available — a complete, version-pinned recipe is present and linked to the claimed evidence and action. Not that it ran.
recipe_reproduced — a verifier reproduced the sealed output from the recipe. Not historical occurrence.
historical_execution_established — true only via a valid observed-execution witness attestation. Never inferred from reproduction.

cards.title: Reported separately from the five propositions
items: external time bounds (Anchoring) — UPPER_ONLY from RFC 3161, LOWER_ONLY from a published beacon, BOUNDED where both resolve. Not the record's content.
completeness and disclosure — completeness asks whether the supplied chain is whole; disclosure asks whether it is the whole assignment. Both default to UNCHECKED without an outside checkpoint.

cards.title: Non-implication rule
items: No claim upgrades another. Each is established on its own evidence.
Reproduction does not prove historical execution.
A valid chain does not prove the disclosed set is whole.
The five propositions are boolean: ESTABLISHED or NOT ESTABLISHED, per EvidencePropositions.
UNCHECKED is the honest default for completeness and disclosure only. It is not a fourth value on every proposition.

cards.title: The wedge, and its likely first result
items: Configuration sits with the provider and is overwritten on revision.
The lender cannot timestamp what it does not hold.

Likely first integration establishes precedence and witness_attestation only where a cooperating provider commits to a configuration digest at execution time. Absent that cooperation, none of the claims can be established for that configuration.
That is a gap in what the provider makes available, not a value this instrument computes.

cards.title: Claim status, distinct from build status
items: FACT — a real execution-evidence problem exists.
FACT — workflows exist where the operator cannot reconstruct execution state.
THESIS — independent custody establishes more than logging or timestamping.
HYPOTHESIS — a party bearing the loss will pay in advance to preserve it.
UNKNOWN — whether any provider will expose a configuration digest at execution.

cards.title: Open, and named rather than hidden
items: Capture exists as an opt-in scaffold; nothing enforces that every run reaches it.
Boundary establishment: nothing prevents execution outside the instrumented path.
Who the witness is, and whether anyone checks what they signed.
Money is spent because this evidence is absent. Established.
That spend converts into a pre-loss purchase. Untested.
